chapters.title: Queen Vashti refuses
chapters.summary: At a lavish feast, King Ahasuerus of Persia orders Queen Vashti to display her beauty. She refuses, and he removes her as queen.

chapters.title: Esther becomes queen
chapters.summary: Esther, a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, is chosen as the new queen without revealing her people. Mordecai uncovers a plot to kill the king.

chapters.title: Haman's plot
chapters.summary: Mordecai refuses to bow to the powerful Haman. In fury Haman gets the king to issue a decree to destroy all the Jews in the empire on a single day.

chapters.title: For such a time as this
chapters.summary: Mordecai urges Esther to plead with the king, though it could cost her life: who knows whether you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this? She asks the Jews to fast.

chapters.title: Esther's request
chapters.summary: Esther approaches the king uninvited and he holds out his scepter. She invites him and Haman to a banquet, while Haman builds a gallows for Mordecai.

chapters.title: Mordecai honored
chapters.summary: Sleepless, the king learns that Mordecai once saved his life. Haman, coming to ask for Mordecai's death, is ordered to honor him publicly instead.

chapters.title: Haman's fall
chapters.summary: At Esther's second banquet she reveals her people and Haman's plot. The king has Haman hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.

chapters.title: A new decree
chapters.summary: Mordecai is given Haman's position. Since the first decree cannot be revoked, a new one lets the Jews defend themselves, and there is joy and gladness.

chapters.title: The Jews defend themselves
chapters.summary: On the appointed day the Jews overcome their enemies. The feast of Purim is established to remember how sorrow was turned to joy.

chapters.title: Mordecai's greatness
chapters.summary: Mordecai becomes second only to the king, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to them.
